extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology from primary text and figures, with efficacy and safety context kept separate from direct mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: VW5 has source-supported membrane interaction and permeabilization evidence in Pseudomonas aeruginosa ATCC 27853 assays, including LPS binding, NPN outer-membrane uptake, and membrane-potential depolarization readouts.

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=3:Figure 3; xml:sec=10:LPS Binding; xml:sec=11:Outer Membrane Permeabilization; xml:sec=12:Cytoplasmic Membrane Depolarization

mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct mechanism evidence is centered on VW5 and tested bacterial membrane assays; it is not generalized to all designed peptides without assay support.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: VW5 causes visible bacterial envelope damage at MIC conditions in source-located scanning and transmission electron microscopy assays for P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 and S. aureus ATCC 29213.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Microscopy supports membrane disruption morphology at tested MIC conditions; it does not quantify every intermediate step of killing.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: VW5 shows source-supported in vivo efficacy context in the mouse cutaneous abscess model, reducing bacterial burden, lesion area, and inflammatory cytokine levels without overt skin toxicity in the reported assays.

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=4:Figure 4; xml:sec=16:Assessment of Bacterial Infection; xml:sec=37:Toxicity of VW5 to Normal Skin Tissue

mechanism_claims.limitations: In vivo efficacy and toxicity context is not treated as a separate molecular mechanism.

caution_findings.finding: Mechanism claims are limited to VW5 and the directly tested assays; other analogues remain activity/toxicity records unless directly assayed.
